title: A terminal you can use all day
description: Shells, tabs, split panes, search, themes and sessions that come back after a restart.

title: Exit codes and timings per command
description: Each command shows how long it took and whether it failed, so you can spot problems in a long session.

title: SSH in a tab
description: Open a remote shell with the host's key checked first.

title: Windows shells tested by hand
description: PowerShell, cmd and WSL checked on a real Windows machine, not only in automated builds.

title: Remote files over SSH
description: Browse, edit and transfer files on a remote machine from the same tab.

title: Connect Claude, OpenAI, Gemini or any OpenAI-compatible service
description: Add your own key, test the connection, and switch models per task.

title: Dedicated OpenRouter integration
description: Model discovery with pricing and capabilities, favourites, provider routing, privacy controls and budgets. Basic use through the OpenAI-compatible connection already works.
note: Basic connection implemented; dedicated integration planned, high priority.

title: Use local models
description: Ollama and LM Studio are detected on your machine and work offline.

title: Coding sessions with Ask, Plan, Build, Debug and Review
description: Every change is shown as a diff before it is applied. Commands run only with your approval.

title: See what leaves your machine
description: A preview of exactly what will be sent to a provider, before it is sent.

title: Memory you control
description: What an agent remembers is scoped to you, the project or a task, and you can see and delete it.

title: Built-in code editor
description: Open, edit and diff files next to the terminal. Saves never overwrite changes made outside Vekrun.

title: Use coding-agent subscriptions you already have
description: Sign in with an existing Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI account where a supported method exists.

title: Diagnostics in the editor
description: Errors and navigation from language servers while you edit.

title: Download local models from inside Vekrun
description: Pick a model that fits your hardware and get it without leaving the app.

title: Board with Start Work
description: A Kanban of your tickets. Start Work opens a branch, a worktree and a terminal, or hands the ticket to an agent or an AI team.

title: GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Jira and Asana tickets on the Board
description: Assigned tickets from every connected tracker in one place, each with Start Work.
note: Adapters and Start Work exist; live provider sync and status updates are not yet verified.

title: Status updates sent back to your tracker
description: When you deliver, the ticket moves and the pull request is linked, with your approval. The sync engine and link-back comments exist; live tracker runs are next.
note: Sync engine and link-back comments exist; verification against live trackers is outstanding.

title: Drag and drop, saved views and a team board
description: Rearrange tickets, keep filters, and see your team's work next to your own.

title: Agents that use your other tools
description: Any MCP server you configure, plus nineteen ready-made presets with sign-in, each with permissions per tool.
note: The client, presets and sign-in exist; the presets are not yet run against the live services.

title: Turn an idea into a plan
description: A structured plan with steps, files and acceptance criteria, which you approve before anything runs.

title: Ask several models to challenge a decision
description: Independent takes, critique rounds and a summary that records where they disagreed.

title: Delegate to a coordinated team
description: A manager splits the work, agents build in separate branches, and a different agent verifies before you review.

title: One inbox for everything waiting on you
description: Approvals, questions and reviews from every running agent, in priority order.

title: Work that continues after you close the window
description: A headless worker picks up tasks and keeps running after you close the window, and picks up where it left off after a restart.

title: Run agents on another machine
description: A remote Vekrun on a workstation or server you control, reached over an SSH tunnel, with reconnect and live logs.

title: Scheduled and recurring tasks
description: Run a workflow on a schedule, on an interval, or when something happens in your repository, with missed-run policies and daily limits.

title: Budgets that agents cannot exceed
description: Limits on tokens, spend, time and tool calls per project and per task, with warn, ask, pause and stop thresholds.

title: Built-in workflows
description: Feature, bug fix, review, documentation, tests, release prep and dependency audit as ready-made team workflows, plus validated imports.

title: Steer a running team
description: Pause, resume, redirect or reassign a task mid-flight, and see exactly what is and is not undone.

title: Agent services and an API
description: Define versioned agent services, invoke them from other agents or your own tools through a scoped, private API, and follow their runs.

title: AI review of your local changes
description: Ask a model to look for problems in a branch or diff before you open a pull request.

title: Compare findings from several models
description: Run a review council on a contested change and see where the models agree and disagree.

title: Review with AI on a teammate’s pull request
description: Findings at exact code locations, verified problems separated from hypotheses, with the option to compare several models.
note: The review engine exists for local branches; running it on a pull request from the inbox is planned.

title: Review Inbox for GitHub pull requests and GitLab merge requests
description: Everything requesting your review, assigned to you or opened by you, with CI status, draft state and linked issues, in Vekrun.
note: High priority. Not started in source.

title: Approve, request changes and comment from Vekrun
description: Inline comments and a verdict submitted through GitHub or GitLab, with AI findings you can edit or dismiss first.
note: High priority. Link-back comments after delivery exist; review submission is not started.

title: Connect monitoring platforms
description: Honeybadger, Sentry, Datadog and AppSignal with read-only tokens in your keychain.
note: All four adapters exist and are tested against recorded responses; none has run against a live account yet.

title: Investigate application errors
description: Inspect exceptions, stack traces, occurrences and a timeline, then ask a read-only agent for likely causes with evidence.
note: Works against recorded provider data in the development build.

title: Find performance bottlenecks
description: Slow requests and the slowest endpoints by p95 from the providers that expose them, with a measured-versus-hypothesised rule.
note: Datadog endpoints and Sentry performance issues exist; trace search and latency observation are outstanding.

title: Create engineering work
description: One ticket per issue in any connected tracker with a duplicate check, or a fix plan with the issue as context.

title: Delegate repairs
description: The incident workflow on an AI team: investigate, reproduce, plan, implement, test, verify, review. Nothing deploys.

title: Verify production improvements
description: Mark a deploy, or let a Sentry release, Honeybadger deploy or AppSignal marker anchor it, and compare the same window before and after.
note: Verdicts come from recorded provider data until live runs pass.

title: Supervised triage of new critical errors
description: Optional. Supervised mode can start an investigation on its own; it never creates tickets or changes code without you.

title: More monitoring providers
description: Grafana Cloud, New Relic, Elastic, OpenSearch, Bugsnag and Rollbar through the same workspace.

title: Incident management
description: PagerDuty and incident.io incidents as investigations with follow-up tickets. Acknowledging or closing an incident stays yours.

title: Feature flags and analytics context
description: Correlate a rollout from LaunchDarkly, PostHog or GrowthBook with the errors or latency that followed. Vekrun never changes a flag.

title: Turn failed builds into fixes
description: Open a failed GitHub Actions run, see which job and test broke, and work on a repair in Vekrun.

title: GitLab CI/CD pipelines
description: Failed pipelines and jobs with their logs, linked to the merge request.

title: AI-assisted test failure repair
description: A repair plan from the failure, then manual, agent or team execution, local tests, and the next CI result.

title: Local Docker development environments
description: Start the services a project needs, run tests inside them and clean up afterwards, with your Docker.

title: Framework-aware testing
description: Playwright, Vitest, Jest, pytest, RSpec and Cypress with parsed results and failure summaries as verification evidence.

title: See deployments where you code
description: Vercel, Cloudflare Workers and Pages, Railway, Render and Fly.io deployments with their status and logs.

title: Know what happened after deployment
description: Connect a release to the code change and observe the production signals that follow.
note: Deployment markers from Sentry, Honeybadger and AppSignal already anchor Insights observations.

title: Authorised deployment actions
description: Deploy only when you say so. Nothing deploys because an agent or a team finished.

title: Find an issue. Prepare a fix. Verify it.
description: Findings from GitHub Code Scanning, Semgrep, SonarQube and Snyk with exact locations, a repair plan and a reviewable change.

title: Independent verification of security fixes
description: A separate agent checks the repair; nothing is marked fixed without verification and no finding is suppressed.

title: Sign in with your own application
description: OAuth with PKCE for the services that allow it, tokens in your keychain, refreshed for you.
note: Tested against Vekrun’s own server and recorded responses.

title: Extensions
description: Manifests, permission review, and extensions that add tools and workflow templates.

title: Webhooks and triggers
description: Signed webhooks on a worker you run, Git and CI hooks, and manual triggers that create tasks or run workflows.

title: Knowledge and collaboration sources
description: Microsoft Teams, Google Drive and OpenAPI specifications as context for plans and investigations.

title: Database connections
description: Neon, PlanetScale, Redis, MongoDB Atlas, AWS RDS and Firebase, read-only by default.

title: Unified Cloud accounts
description: One Vekrun account for the desktop application and the browser dashboard, used to join organizations.
note: Cloud sign-in never grants access to repositories or other services on its own; those connections are authorized separately.

title: Email and social sign-in
description: Sign in with email, Google, GitHub or GitLab.

title: Organization creation, invitations and multiple memberships
description: Create an organization, invite teammates, assign roles and belong to more than one organization with the same account.

title: Organization workspace in the desktop app
description: Join an organization from the same Vekrun you already use, and switch between your personal workspace and each organization without reinstalling or losing personal projects.

title: Selective synchronization
description: Choose what an organization workspace shares: tickets, assignments, plans, approval records, review status and approved execution summaries, according to organization policy. Personal projects and personal credentials stay in your local store; source code is not uploaded for coordination.

title: Shared Board workflows, projects and plans
description: Projects, ticket assignments, plans and Insights investigations shared across the developers in an organization, on the same Board they already use.

title: Shared Factory queue
description: Organization-wide Factory queues, approved shared workers, job progress, verification results and execution history visible to the team.
note: The same Vekrun AI engine runs local and organization work; no separate agent engine or proprietary model is required.

title: Centralized approvals
description: Plans, merges, expensive AI operations, permission requests and sensitive actions routed to the person an organization policy names, with the context to decide.

title: Team review coordination
description: Review requests routed to teammates, AI-assisted findings shared with the reviewer, and project status updated when a pull request merges.

title: Project manager web dashboard
description: A browser view of projects, work in progress, blocked tasks, pending reviews, AI operations, quality and delivered work, with no desktop install needed.

title: Engineering reports
description: Completed work, delivery trends, review bottlenecks, agent usage and engineering spending per project and team.

title: Organization-level AI policies and governance
description: Roles and permissions, allowed models and providers, spending limits, approval requirements, shared worker permissions, audit history and data-sharing policies.

title: Enterprise SSO
description: SAML and OIDC single sign-on with enforcement for an organization.

title: SCIM provisioning
description: Members and teams provisioned from the company directory.

title: Advanced access control, audit exports and private deployment
description: Custom roles and per-repository rules, exportable audit history and private deployment options for Enterprise organizations.

title: Commercial billing
description: Subscriptions for organizations and their management. Nothing can be bought until this exists, and Community stays free.

title: Signed installers for macOS, Windows and Linux
description: Public builds with checksums and a working update path.

title: Guided first run
description: Pick a shell and a theme, then connect AI or skip it.
